Q: How to find a resource file with pyaims using the BrainVISA suite of software? A:

There is a function, called findResourceFile, that permits to do just this:

from soma import aims

lpath = aims.carto.Paths.findResourceFile(
        'models/models_2008/descriptive_models/segments'
        '/global_registered_spam_left/meshes/Lspam_model_meshes_1.arg')
print(f"Path to resource = {lpath}")
a = aims.read(lpath)

Q: Simultaneous access to a table in a shared folder A:

We have a solution at work where everyone has a client side Excel file that takes care of the writing to a server side Excel file.
Obviously there can be occasions where two people want to write at the same time but that can be handled with a "is file already open? yes: wait a little, try again" loop for 5 times.

So far it works fine here. Last year's file has 45811 lines of data and I can't remember there being any major issues.

Q: How to match any amount of Unicode characters (letters, numbers, surrogate pairs) in regex? A:

First of all Sutrrogate Pairs are a UTF-16 phenomenon when joined ,
(via bit-rolls and masks) form a Code Point past the BMP > U+00FFFF.
So the full range of valid Unicode Code Points are from U+000000 - U+10FFFF.

That's a lot of characters. 1,114,111 (Dec) of them.
Not all are usable. just using a regex [\x{0}-\x{10ffff}] should cover it.

However these are the Printable ones :

[^\p{NChar}\p{Cc}\p{Cn}\p{Cs}\p{Co}]

AKA Long Names: [^\p{Noncharacter_Code_Point}\p{Control}\p{Unassigned}\p{Surrogate}\p{Private_Use}]

To exclude non-chars, private use and unassignrd the regex is :
[^\p{NChar}\p{Cn}\p{Co}]

https://regex101.com/r/U8xZmi/1

This results in a set of 157,110 usable characters (not including U+00) as of Unicode 16

Q: New Google Sheets custom functions sometimes display "Loading..." indefinitely A:

Same problem here in 2025

The most often reason - some issue on servers (google side). This means fix can not work.

Strategy to try:

  1. at the beginning of function thow own error like this: throw "👀Please wait...Dev is testing this function"
  2. Delete formula and enter it again. See the red triangle now must show your custom error instead.
  3. Delete your error (1), repeat step (2) again. Hope it will fix the issue.

For me it worked.

Q: Hash string into RGB color A:

Since the question is tagged "language agnostic", here it is on linux shell (inspired by https://stackoverflow.com/a/20109176/32273721):

md5sum <<<"mystring" | sed -r 's;^(.{6}).*;#\1;'

Output:

#1e6f40

I'm using this to programmatically color Graphviz graphs nodes/edges.

Q: Selenium opening browser very slowly on Mac A:

The slowness you’re seeing when opening a browser on Mac is a common issue, and it’s usually not caused by selenium itself, but by how the driver interacts with the browser and the OS. Here are the key points:

1. Use the correct driver for your OS

In your example, you are using a windows Edge driver path:

PATH = 'C:/Users/a0952/edgedriver_win64/msedgedriver.exe'

This path obviously won’t work on a Mac. On macOS, you need the macOS EdgeDriver (or ChromeDriver if using Chrome). For Chrome:

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

chrome_options = Options()
chrome_options.add_argument("--start-maximized")
chrome_options.add_argument("--disable-extensions")
chrome_options.add_argument("--disable-gpu")
chrome_options.add_argument("--no-sandbox")  # sometimes needed on Mac
chrome_options.add_argument("--headless")    # optional: runs without opening UI

service = Service('/path/to/chromedriver')  # macOS path
driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=service, options=chrome_options)

driver.get('http://www.google.com')
driver.quit()

Make sure your driver is executable on macOS:

chmod +x /path/to/chromedriver

2. Update WebDriver & Browser

Make sure both your Edge/Chrome and driver are up to date. Mismatched versions often cause delays or instability.

3. Consider the browser startup overhead

Browsers on macOS (especially Edge/Chrome) can take a few seconds to start, even without Selenium. This is normal. If you want to measure actual page automation speed, you can run Chrome in headless mode (--headless), which usually starts faster.

Q: Can't select Python interpreter in Cursor, even though it exists A:

it is annoying, the code runs, and everything works fine, but the cursor can't see the interpreter, making it even show a linter configuration issue like (import of Matplotlib can't be solved).

Solution partially would be:

using the code runner extension type ctrl +shit+x and, install it, and put the interpreter manually in setting.

{

"code-runner.runInTerminal":True

"python.defaultInterpreterPath":" Your path of anaconda or python in users folder usually"

}

You might need to add code-runner-executionMap also for code runner extension.
